## Create Table for Regressions

### Helper Functions

```{python}
def county_average(df, include_cols = None):
    if "county_id" not in df.columns:
        raise ValueError("No `county_id` column found.")

    if include_cols is None:
        include_cols = [
            col for col in df.columns
            if col != "county_id" and is_numeric_dtype(df[col])
        ]
    else:
        non_num_cols = [
            col for col in include_cols 
            if col =="county_id" or not is_numeric_dtype(df[col])
            ]
        if non_num_cols:
            raise ValueError(f"Only numeric columns are allowed in `include_cols`. Non-numeric columns: {non_num_cols}")

    # Since there are no years for datacenters, take average of all years for each county
    out_df = (df[["county_id"] + include_cols].groupby("county_id", as_index = False).mean())

    return out_df
```

```{python}
def combine_dfs(base_df, dfs_to_join):
    out_df = base_df.copy()

    for i, df in enumerate(dfs_to_join):
        if "county_id" not in df.columns:
            raise ValueError(f"No `county_id` column found in dfs_to_join[{i}]")

        # Make sure all tables only have one row per county
        dupes = df["county_id"][df[["county_id","year"]].duplicated()].unique()
        if len(dupes) > 0:
            raise ValueError(f"dfs_to_join[{i}] is not unique on `county_id and year`. Problematic Counties: {list(dupes)}")

        out_df = pd.merge(out_df, df, how = "left", on = ["county_id", "year"], validate = "one_to_one")

    missing_summary_table = (
        out_df.isna()
        .mean()
        .sort_values(ascending = False)
        .rename("missing_share")
        .reset_index()
        .rename(columns={"index":"column"})
    )

    print("Missing Summary: \n", missing_summary_table)

    return out_df
```

### Create final table

### Clean up final table

```{python}
# Make applicable columns per-capita
bus_cols = ["tot_employee_count", "annual_payroll", "tot_establishment_count"]

cols = [c for c in final_df.columns if any(l in c for l in bus_cols)]

per_capita_cols = [
    "real_gdp_2017_dollars_thousands",
    "real_gdp_2017_dollars_thousands_spatial_weighted_avg_5",
    "personal_income_thousands_of_dollars",
    "personal_income_thousands_of_dollars_spatial_weighted_avg_5",
    "all_permits",
    "all_permits_spatial_weighted_avg_5",
    "single_family_permits",
    "single_family_permits_spatial_weighted_avg_5",
    "all_multifamily_permits",
    "all_multifamily_permits_spatial_weighted_avg_5"
] + cols

final_df = mlu.make_per_capita(final_df, per_capita_cols)
```

```{python}
# Per-capita data centers (don't drop original though)
final_df["datacenters_per_capita"] = final_df["estabs"] / final_df["population"]
final_df["datacenters_spatial_per_capita"] = final_df["estabs_spatial_weighted_avg_5"] / final_df["population"]
```

```{python}
# Rename for clarity
final_df = final_df.rename(columns = {
    "annual_payroll_per_capita": "annual_payroll_thousands_per_capita", 
    "estabs": "datacenters",
    "estabs_spatial_weighted_avg_5": "datacenters_spatial_weighted_avg_5",
    "unemployment_rate": "unemployment_rate_pct"
    })

# Drop temporal columns as the regression model should be able to handle this without needing extra columns
final_df = final_df.drop(columns = final_df.columns[final_df.columns.str.contains("yoy", case=False)])

final_df = final_df.sort_values(["county_id", "year"]).reset_index(drop=True)
```
